facts.statement: Daemonosaurus was an extinct dinosaur from the Late Triassic period found in New Mexico.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus is an extinct genus of possible theropod dinosaur from the Late Triassic of New Mexico.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Daemonosaurus consists of a skull and neck fragments found at Ghost Ranch.
facts.quote: The only known fossil is a skull and neck fragments from deposits of the latest Triassic Chinle Formation at Ghost Ranch.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus had a short skull and large, fang-like teeth.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus was an unusual dinosaur with a short skull and large, fang-like teeth.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus likely lies outside the Neotheropoda clade due to retaining primitive snout traits.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus retains several plesiomorphic ("primitive") traits of the snout, and it likely lies outside the clade Neotheropoda.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus was named by Sues, Nesbitt, Berman, and Henrici in 2011.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus was named by Hans-Dieter Sues, Sterling J. Nesbitt, David S. Berman and Amy C. Henrici in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B in 2011

facts.statement: The name Daemonosaurus means "demon reptile" derived from Greek words.
facts.quote: The generic name Daemonosaurus is derived from the Greek words "daimon" (δαίμων) meaning "demon" and "sauros" (σαύρα) meaning "reptile".

facts.statement: The species name chauliodus means "prominent toothed" referring to its forward-pointing front teeth.
facts.quote: The specific name is derived from the Greek word "chauliodous" (χαυλιόδους) meaning "prominent toothed", which is in reference to its procumbent front teeth.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in a sediment block from the Coelophysis Quarry at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
facts.quote: This specimen was discovered in a sediment block of collected from the Coelophysis Quarry (also known as the Whitaker quarry) at Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.

facts.statement: The fossil block containing the holotype was collected in the early 1980s by E.H. Colbert.
facts.quote: C-4-81, the block containing CM 76821, was collected in the early 1980s by E.H. Colbert

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was first uncovered by a volunteer while the block was on loan to the State Museum of Pennsylvania.
facts.quote: CM 76821 was first uncovered by a volunteer preparing the block while it was on loan to State Museum of Pennsylvania in Harrisburg.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus is characterized by a short, deep skull with large teeth and a rounded eye socket.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus is notable for its short, deep skull, with large teeth, a rounded orbit (eye socket) and a relatively small antorbital fenestra.

facts.statement: Sues estimated Daemonosaurus to be around 1.5 meters long based on related theropod proportions.
facts.quote: Based on the proportions of related theropods, Daemonosaurus is estimated to have been around 1.5 m (5 feet) long according to Sues.

facts.statement: Holtz estimated Daemonosaurus was at most 2.2 meters long and weighed between 9.1 and 22.7 kilograms.
facts.quote: An estimate by Holtz (2012) suggests that Daemonosaurus was at most 2.2 m long with a weight around that of a beaver, 9.1-22.7 kg.

facts.statement: Size estimates for Daemonosaurus are largely conjectural because no postcranial fossils exist beyond a few vertebrae.
facts.quote: These estimates are almost entirely conjectural, as no postcranial fossils are preserved beyond a few vertebrae.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus had only three premaxillary teeth, unlike other early dinosaurs which typically had four.
facts.quote: There are only three premaxillary teeth, like Tawa, Gnathovorax, Heterodontosaurus, and an unnamed Brazilian herrerasaurid, but unlike other early dinosaurs, which have four.

facts.statement: The first premaxillary tooth in Daemonosaurus was the longest tooth in its entire skull.
facts.quote: The premaxillary teeth are characteristically elongated, with the first tooth being the longest in the entire skull.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus premaxillary teeth were straight at the root and curved at the crown.
facts.quote: The premaxillary teeth are straight at the root and curved at the crown.

facts.statement: The maxilla of Daemonosaurus had at most 10 teeth, fewer than any other known early dinosaur.
facts.quote: The maxilla has 10 teeth at most, fewer than any other early dinosaur.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus had scleral rings in its eyes with at least 11 overlapping ossicles arranged in a counterclockwise pattern.
facts.quote: Scleral rings were present in each eye, with at least 11 ossicles overlapping in a counterclockwise pattern.

facts.statement: The dentary of Daemonosaurus held an estimated ten curved and serrated teeth.
facts.quote: The dentary (tooth-bearing portion of the jaw) has an estimated ten teeth, which are curved and serrated.

facts.statement: In the lower jaw of Daemonosaurus, the second tooth was the largest, followed by a large first tooth inset from the tip, with the rest decreasing in size towards the back.
facts.quote: The first tooth is large and slightly inset from the tip of the jaw, the second tooth is the largest in the lower jaw, and the rest decrease in size to the back of the jaw.

facts.statement: A large oval hole behind the rib articulations in Daemonosaurus has been equated with pneumatic pockets seen in other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: A very large rimmed oval-shaped hole is present behind the rib articulations. This hole has been equated with pneumatic pockets ("pleurocoels") observed in Tawa, Chindesaurus, and neotheropods.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus lived alongside early neotheropods like Coelophysis during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: It lived alongside early neotheropods such as Coelophysis, which would have been among the most common dinosaurs by the end of the Triassic.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Daemonosaurus is a basal theropod or a non-theropod basal saurischian.
facts.quote: It may be considered a late-surviving basal theropod or non-theropod basal saurischian, possibly allied to other early predatory dinosaurs such as herrerasaurids or Tawa.

facts.statement: A 2026 study proposed the clade Morphoraptora to group Daemonosaurus with Tawa and other herrerasaurians.
facts.quote: A 2026 study named the clade Morphoraptora for Daemonosaurus, Tawa, and other proposed herrerasaurians of the southwest United States.

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus is classified as a basal theropod situated outside the Neotheropoda clade.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus is typically considered to be a basal theropod that lies outside the clade Neotheropoda

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis found Daemonosaurus chauliodus to be closely related to Tawa hallae.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus chauliodus to be closely related to Tawa hallae

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus differs from Herrerasaurus by having much larger teeth in the premaxilla and distinct skull features.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus differs from Herrerasaurus based on key features in the skull and because it has much larger teeth in the premaxilla

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus is distinguished from Eoraptor lunensis by possessing much larger premaxillary and anterior maxillary teeth.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus differs from Eoraptor lunensis based on the presence of much larger premaxillary and anterior maxillary teeth

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus differs from Chindesaurus bryansmalli based on features of its cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus differs from Chindesaurus bryansmalli in features of the cervical vertebrae

facts.statement: Nesbitt and Sues (2020) considered Daemonosaurus a likely saurischian but could not conclusively place it within any specific dinosaur subgroup.
facts.quote: Nesbitt and Sues (2020) considered Daemonosaurus a likely saurischian, they were unable to conclusively place the genus within any subgroup of Dinosauria

facts.statement: Recent studies recovered Daemonosaurus in a clade named Morphoraptora alongside Tawa, Chindesaurus, and Ptychotherates.
facts.quote: Novas et al. (2021) and Strivastava and Nesbitt (2026) recovered Daemonosaurus in a clade (which the latter study named Morphoraptora)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Daemonosaurus as Saurischia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saurischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Daemonosaurus is Daemonosaurus chauliodus.
facts.quote: Type species: Daemonosaurus chauliodus

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Daemonosaurus was found at the Whitaker quarry in Ghost Ranch, New Mexico.
facts.quote: The only specimen of Daemonosaurus was recovered at the Coelophysis (Whitaker) quarry at Ghost Ranch in Rio Arriba County, New Mexico

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically the Rhaetian stage or possibly the latest Norian stage.
facts.quote: It has been correlated the Siltstone Member of the Chinle Formation, which is tentatively dated to the Rhaetian (or possibly latest Norian) stage of the Late Triassic period

facts.statement: 200 million years ago, the habitat of Daemonosaurus near the equator featured a warm, monsoon-like climate with heavy seasonal rain.
facts.quote: Ghost Ranch was located close to the equator 200 million years ago, and had a warm, monsoon-like climate with heavy seasonal precipitation

facts.statement: Fossil evidence suggests Daemonosaurus died after being washed into a pond and drowned during a sheet flood event.
facts.quote: In 1989, Colbert noted that the Daemonosaurus specimen and several Coelophysis specimens were washed into a small pond, where they drowned and were buried by a sheet flood event from a nearby river

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus lived between 205.7 and 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Rhaetian to Rhaetian (205.7 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Daemonosaurus represents a lineage from the earliest dinosaur radiation that persisted alongside South American forms like Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus until the end of the Triassic.
facts.quote: Daemonosaurus represents a lineage that extended from the earliest radiation of dinosaurs in the Middle Triassic alongside forms such as Eoraptor and Herrerasaurus from South America

rejected.statement: The prefrontal bone in Daemonosaurus was proportionally large, forming about half the upper edge of the orbit.
rejected.quote: The prefrontal is proportionally large, forming about half the upper edge of the orbit.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'proportionally large forming about half the upper edge'

rejected.statement: In one hypothesis, Baron et al. (2017) classified Daemonosaurus as the earliest ornithischian, though it retained many theropod-like traits.
rejected.quote: Daemonosaurus was found to be the earliest ornithischian, retaining many theropod-like characteristics
